findings.card_says: Transmission "was transferred from [the VRA] to the Ghana Grid Company Limited between 2009 and 2010 following the amendment of the Volta River Authority Act in 2005"; GRIDCo "created out of the Volta River Authority, which took over the project and the transmission assets during 2009 and 2010".
findings.writer_reported: GRIDCo's 2023 annual report gives incorporation December 2006 and operations from August 2008, which should be read against the card's 2009-2010 window.
findings.why: No conflict, and the card is cited correctly. The completion report paragraph 42 says "The principal FM challenge for the Ghana component was the transition from VRA management to GRIDCo, which took place between 2009 and 2010", and paragraph 20(a) says the December 2010 restructuring "formally transferred the corresponding project obligations from the VRA to GRIDCo" after GRIDCo "assumed the VRA's transmission assets". The 2005 Act amendment is in the other cited document: the resettlement action plan addendum's introduction reads "with the formation of the Ghana Grid Company (GRIDCo) following the amendment of the VRA Act 46 in 2005, the transmission component has been hived from VRA to GRIDCo". Incorporation and becoming operational are not the asset or obligation transfer, so GRIDCo's own dates sit alongside the card rather than against it. Recorded for completeness: the appraisal document adds a fifth date, "In 1997, VRA registered a wholly owned subsidiary company - the National Grid Company Ltd (GRIDCO) as a first step towards enhancing the operational autonomy of the transmission system operation", and says that as at appraisal "VRA has not transferred transmission and load dispatch assets to that subsidiary company".

findings.card_says: "The state body that then held Tanzania's railway land"; "because the land belonged to RAHCO the affected people were paid for improvements on the land only and not for the land".
findings.writer_reported: The Railways Act 2002 does not say RAHCO owned railway land, so the card's phrase is thinner in the statute; separately, the Act was repealed on 28 February 2018 by the Railways Act 2017.
findings.verdict: rejected as to the land, confirmed as to the repeal
findings.why: The land claim is sourced correctly to the document the card cites, and the statute's silence is not a contradiction. TANESCO's January 2014 amendment says in its own words, at section 2.3 Ukonga: "All (PAPs) requested TANESCO to help them in paying compensation of properties excluding land because the land belongs to RAHCO", and "The Managing Director approved the decision to undertake valuation of properties and compensate PAPs for exhausted improvements only made on land within the said wayleave corridor of RAHCO". The writer is right that the 2002 Act says nothing about owning railway land, and the description does not repeat it; but the Act does reserve a railway strip of 15 metres in urban and 30 metres in rural areas within which building needs the company's written permission (ss.4, 57) and provides for compensation on acquisition (s.44(3)-(4)), so the statute is not inconsistent with the card either. No card edit. The repeal is confirmed: TanzLII's note on the 2002 Act reads "This Act was repealed on 2018-02-28 by Railways Act"; the 2017 Act was assented 8 October 2017, published in Gazette 41 of 13 October 2017, establishes the Tanzania Railways Corporation at s.4(1), and its commencements table gives 28 February 2018 for s.113 "Repeal and savings" and 30 June 2018 for ss.114 and 116, both by Government Notice 65 of 2018.
documents: TANESCO, Amendment of Resettlement Action Plan, January 2014, s.2.3 (cached P101645_RAP, lines 155-180)
Railways Act 2002, TanzLII, repeal note and ss.4, 6, 7(3), 44, 57
Railways Act 2017, TanzLII PDF, cover, s.4(1), commencements table

findings.card_says: CEB as the binational utility selling to SBEE and CEET.
findings.writer_reported: A September 2015 Financial Afrik headline says the CEB lost its exclusivity in purchasing electricity; not opened, flagged as a lead.
findings.why: The article was opened and it reports a step short of an enacted change. It says Togo's Council of Ministers adopted, on 2 September 2015, a projet de loi removing the provisions of the Benin-Togo electricity code agreement that made CEB the sole buyer, which the government said "ouvre ainsi le marché de l'énergie à la concurrence dans nos deux pays", and quotes the communiqué that CEB's monopoly rights "se limitent désormais aux importations, à ses propres sources de production et au transport". No amended code, enacted law or Benin-side instrument was opened, and the code as ratified by Benin in 2005 still gives CEB transport, importation and single-buyer exclusivity at article L5. So something was in train in 2015 that would narrow the exclusivity, and it cannot be dated or confirmed as law here. The CEB description now states the exclusivity as the 2005 code states it and claims nothing current. No card edit.

findings.card_says: NTDC as one of two further state-owned implementing agencies.
findings.writer_reported: NEPRA's Modification-III, approved March 2023, removes system-operator functions from transmission licence TL/01/2002, to be licensed separately under section 23G, with legal separation required within two years.
findings.why: The determination was downloaded and read. Its registrar's letter is dated March 21, 2023; its background records that TL/01/2002 of December 31, 2002 gave NTDC exclusivity as National Grid Company for the functions of Transmission Network Operator and System Operator "in the whole country except for the service area of K-Electric Limited (KEL)"; and it approves the modification "to the extent of exclusion of functions of System Operator and revision of terms and conditions of the Transmission Licence", to come into force from the effective date of System Operator Licence No. SOL/01/2023. Clause 19.2 of the modified licence requires separation of the System Operator functions "not later than two (02) years from the effective date of the System Operator Licence". The State of Industry Report 2023 confirms the grant and adds a date and term: NTDC applied on August 24, 2022 and "the Authority after due diligence granted the same to NTDC on March 21, 2023 for a term of twenty (20) years". Recorded as a source-internal inconsistency in the regulator's own report: at section 2.2.10 the same report says "NEPRA has therefore granted licence to NPCC to act as an independent System Operator" and calls the legal separation of NPCC from NTDC essential, while its regulatory-activities section heads the item "Grant of System Operator Licence to NTDC". Both are given and neither is reconciled. No card edit: the change post-dates the 2014 completion report, and it is now carried in the description.

Its arrangement of sections has two items, "Commencement" and "Amendment of section 77 of Act 1 of 2011". Its long title is "An Act to amend section 77 of the Kampala Capital City Act, 2010 to empower the Minister responsible for the Capital City, in consultation with the Minister responsible for finance and the Minister responsible for the public service, to determine the remuneration payable to the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Council of Kampala Capital City Authority and speakers and deputy speakers of division urban councils", and section 1 deems the offices to have come into force on 1 February 2020. findings.card_says: "Sierra Leone's state electricity distribution utility, successor to the National Power Authority, which owns the Freetown distribution network the project upgraded".
findings.writer_reported: not reported by the writer; found on this check, after the statute was recovered
findings.verdict: confirmed, and a card edit is proposed
findings.why: The National Electricity Act 2011 does repeal the National Power Authority Act 1982 (s.82(1)) and transfer National Power Authority employees to "the Company or Authority" on commencement (s.77(a)), so "successor" is right; but it splits the predecessor between two bodies, because s.2 establishes the Sierra Leone Electricity Generation and Transmission Company and its functions include to "own and operate the existing generating assets of the National Power Authority", while EDSA gets supply, distribution and retail sale under s.34. The card's bare "successor" reads as sole succession. The edit above is offered rather than applied; the statute is in the description either way. The 2022 World Bank stakeholder plan the entry also cites does state in section 1.3 that the main grid and isolated grids are ones "EDSA owns and operates", which supports the card's ownership of the Freetown network, and that document does not call EDSA the National Power Authority's successor at all.
documents: The National Electricity Act, 2011 (No. 16 of 2011), ss.2, 25, 34, 77, 82 (sierra-leone.org/Laws/2011-16.pdf, read by OCR)
The National Electricity (Amendment) Act, 2018 (No. 3 of 2018), ss.1-2
